'''Arthur David Yaghjian''' (born January 1, 1943)<ref name="incremental"/> is an American electrical engineer who is best known for his contributions to [[electromagnetic theory]] and its applications.

==Education and career==
A native of [[Providence, Rhode Island]],<ref name="incremental"/> Yaghjian received B.S. (1964), M.S.(1966) and Ph.D.(1969) degrees in electrical engineering from [[Brown University]]. After working as an instructor at [[Tougaloo College]] and [[Hampton University]], he joined the electromagnetics division of the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] in 1971. In 1983, he became a research scientist at the electromagnetics directorate of the [[Air Force Research Laboratory]], where he worked until 1996. He held guest professorships at [[IIT Kharagpur]] (1987), [[Technical University of Denmark]] (1989) and [[University of Siena]] (2007).<ref name="ieee-aps-2"/> 

Yaghjian's contributions include probe-compensated [[Electromagnetic radiation#Near and far fields|near-field]] [[antenna measurement]]s, theory of electromagnetic fields in [[metamaterial]]s, [[dyadic Green's function]]s and analysis of electrically small [[Antenna (radio)|antennas]].<ref name="ieee-aps-2"/><ref name="chew"/> 

==Honors==
Yaghjian is a Life Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]]. In 2020, he was awarded an honorary doctorate from the [[Technical University of Denmark]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://electro.dtu.dk/news/nyhed?id=5a5435b5-9b0c-4df4-8aa9-bd513dfc8016|title=Arthur D. Yaghjian receives DTU Honorary Doctor Degree|date=April 26, 2021|publisher=Technical University of Denmark Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering|access-date=2025-02-25}}</ref> Yaghjian received the 2021 IEEE APS Distinguished Achievement Award.<ref name="ieee-aps-2"/><ref name="ieee-aps"/> In 2022, he received the [[IEEE Electromagnetics Award]] "for contributions to fundamental electromagnetic theory and its applications to near-field antenna measurements."<ref name="ieee-electromagnetics"/>
